title: A registered run's verification record settles, but no settlement notice reaches the requesting session, which keeps waiting
outcome: A registered run's verification record settles, but no settlement notice reaches the requesting session, which keeps waiting
acceptance: When a registered run's verification record settles (passed or failed), the requesting session's next turn carries a settlement notice naming the record, even if the run's earlier notice was already delivered, and a session waiting on that run through a run wait is resumed with a prompt that names the settled record; covered by behaviour tests for a failed run. One limit applies to run waits: if the host's look leaves the record pending for a reason under which it is not sent or settled, namely a route reason (no_connection, capability_unsupported, initiating_session_gone or persist_failed), a refusal of the record's body or input (such as body_mismatch), or a record Engram has received that this host cannot yet settle because no launch observation carries it, the wait is resumed naming that reason (and, for a received record, its record ids) instead of the settled record, and a later settlement, if any, then reaches only the run owner's next turn, not a different session that was waiting on the run (tracked as w-d73a959467a1). These outcomes assume a run's launcher-written files (its request, results and other run files) are not rewritten or replaced by anything other than the launcher after the run's terminal write; removal of the run directory and files becoming unreadable remain covered, while defence against such rewrites is tracked as w-3c1dd299f0f6.
A session can read a run's settled state through a documented read-only route (for example the launcher's summary) that reports the record id and outcome.
